top3.headline: Anthropic launches Fable 5.2, but says start with Opus 5.5
top3.whyItMatters: Pick models by task: the new flagship is pitched as orchestrator, not default workhorse.

top3.headline: Anthropic's guide: smaller models for subagents, effort before upgrades
top3.whyItMatters: Routing subagents to smaller models is the vendor-backed way to cut agent costs.

top3.headline: OpenAI built a central system to stop risky AI workloads fast
top3.whyItMatters: Any company running agents at scale needs the same: one view, one stop button.

items.title: Verge: what is known about the Nvidia spy scandal targeting Huang
items.takeaway: Stratechery, Gary Marcus and MIT Technology Review also covered the story today.
items.soWhat: Leadership risk at the top AI chip supplier keeps growing; watch your supply exposure.

items.title: Theo: Fable 5.2 built a project in 76 minutes for $42
items.takeaway: He says the result was not significantly better than Opus 5.5, especially for the price.
items.soWhat: Test new flagships on your own work before paying a premium for marginal gains.

items.title: OpenAI builds Control Room to halt risky research workloads fast
items.takeaway: It tracks every research inference workload, including agentic sampling for training and evals, from one place.
items.soWhat: If you run agents at scale, you need one place to see and stop them.

items.title: ClaudeDevs maps when to use Fable, Opus, Sonnet or Haiku
items.takeaway: The guide also covers adjusting effort before switching models, and running subagents on smaller models to save cost.
items.soWhat: Tune effort first and put subagents on smaller models; that is where agent costs fall.

items.title: Matt Pocock: tell the AI the problem, not the feature
items.takeaway: Instead of asking for an admin analytics panel, say admins can't see an overview of the important data.
items.soWhat: Teams get better agent output by framing the user problem instead of dictating the solution.

items.title: Alex Albert's one prompt to audit projects on each new model
items.takeaway: Find what is broken, inconsistent, inefficient or unneeded; fix the sure things and list the rest for review.
items.soWhat: A new model release is a cheap moment to audit code your team already owns.

items.title: MIT Tech Review: data center backlash may be about electricity
items.takeaway: MIT Technology Review argues the backlash about data centers might really just be about electricity.
items.soWhat: Expect local power costs to shape pushback on new AI data centers.

items.title: Anthropic ships Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, up to 30% faster
items.takeaway: Same model under two names; Fable adds cyber and bio safeguards so all users get it. $8/$40 per million tokens.
items.soWhat: Anthropic itself says start with Opus 5.5 and use Fable 5.2 as advisor or orchestrator.

related.name: Ethan Mollick: Fable 5.2 and Jagged AGI

items.title: Meta's small Muse Ember claims near-flagship smarts at 17x less
items.takeaway: Alexandr Wang says it matches Haiku at a third of the cost per task, at $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens.
items.soWhat: Cheap capable models make high-volume agent work affordable; re-price your routine workloads.

items.title: Grok Bot team says it shipped 11,000 PRs last month
items.takeaway: poteto will explain at AI Engineer on Wednesday how the team kept code quality at that volume.
items.soWhat: Agent-scale output is now a team claim; ask what review system keeps that quality real.

items.title: Nancy Pelosi's replacement is ready to regulate AI
items.takeaway: MIT Technology Review reports that Nancy Pelosi's replacement is ready to regulate AI.
items.soWhat: Post-midterm Congress may push AI rules harder; plan compliance before bills arrive.

items.title: Trump's 60 Minutes interview turns to AI safety
items.takeaway: The Verge reports the interview touched on AI safety and a threat to arrest an AI executive.
items.soWhat: AI leaders now face political risk at the very top, not only regulatory risk.

items.title: Nathan Benaich: defenders need open cyber models too
items.takeaway: He says Hugging Face found API guardrails slowed an intrusion probe and used a self-hosted open model.
items.soWhat: Closed-model guardrails can block your own security team; keep an open-model option for incidents.

items.title: Disney and Adobe are building generative AI tools together
items.takeaway: The Verge reports a partnership on generative AI tools between the two companies.
items.soWhat: Major rights holders are choosing licensed creative AI partners over fighting the tools.

items.title: Meng To rebuilds his apartment as a walkable 3D web scene
items.takeaway: Built with Opus 5.5 in three.js for tutorial videos: walkable in the browser, adjustable lighting, render styles, every object defined in code.
items.soWhat: Designers can now build interactive 3D spaces from prompts, without a 3D modeling team.

items.title: Lyn Alden: Japan's real market force is its overseas cash
items.takeaway: Alden says Japan's quiet Godzilla is not the carry trade but its net international investment position, from pensions to private investors.
items.soWhat: Watch Japan's pension and private money abroad, not just the carry trade, for global market risk.

items.title: Garry Tan's evals say the Jev agent-cost article replicates
items.takeaway: His gstack-evals project re-ran the article on cutting agent bills by 90% with Jev Engineering and Kimi K3, and reports it replicates.
items.soWhat: Agent cost claims are getting independent checks; ask vendors for the same before you switch.

related.name: Article: cut your agent bill by 90% with Jev Engineering

items.title: Theo: coding models still botch MCP authentication for agents
items.takeaway: Theo says Opus makes bad assumptions setting up MCP auth and builds something that fails. He is writing his own MCP guide for his agents.
items.soWhat: Have a human review any agent-built MCP auth before it touches production systems.

related.name: Theo: LLMs are still bad at building tools for agents

items.title: Vitalik Buterin: a data center slowdown looks net good
items.takeaway: Vitalik argues algorithmic progress lets today's data centers match bigger ones within about four years, buying time to harden against cyber and bio risks.
items.soWhat: Opposition to data centers now has a capability-neutral case that investors and boards will hear.

voices.quote: Read this entire project and find everything that’s broken, inconsistent, inefficient, or no longer needed. Fix what you’re sure about and list the rest for me to review.
open cyber models can put more powerful tools in attackers’ hands. defenders need those capabilities too.
we are entering a renaissance in programming language and runtime research, and a golden age of software testing and verification. it's time to rewrite all software.
I really hope Jensen stays, he is the champion for open source, and if Nvidia is ruled by corpo ladder climbers instead we are in for very dark days ahead
Every gripe you have about bad managers is a bug report for interacting with agents.

hotOnX.text: Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 are available now.
hotOnX.note: Builders are weighing its speed and price against Opus 5.5 for daily work.

hotOnX.text: Which Claude model to build with: Fable 5.2, Opus 5.5, Sonnet or Haiku, and when to adjust effort instead.
hotOnX.note: Teams want a clear rule for model choice and cost after the launch.

hotOnX.text: The prompt I run on every project with each new model: find what's broken, fix what you're sure about, list the rest.
hotOnX.note: A copyable habit that turns each model release into cleanup time.

hotOnX.text: We built Control Room to track model workloads and stop them quickly when safety or security concerns arise.
hotOnX.note: People want to see how a lab can halt its own agents in practice.

hotOnX.text: Muse Ember: nearly Muse Spark 1.3 (max) intelligence at a 17x cheaper price point.
hotOnX.note: A cheap, capable model could reprice high-volume agent work.
